reponse:
The failure was in `ingest v2.14.0`: it raised the default batch size from 1 MB to 10 MB, but workers still had a 512 MiB memory limit. Large batches exhausted memory, causing worker pods to crash-loop and the pipeline to fall behind. The change went to all pods at once, and we had no alert on consumer lag; the first signal was an out-of-memory alert 27 minutes after deployment. [1]

We found no customer data loss: events continued arriving in Kafka, and reconciliation confirmed the counts matched. Dashboards were stale for 3 hours 40 minutes; the rollback at 10:05 was followed by the backlog clearing at 12:27 UTC. [1]

The batch-size default has been reverted and a memory guard added. The follow-up changes are to page on-call when lag exceeds five minutes, send ingest configuration changes to a canary pool first, raise worker memory to 1 Gi, and add load tests for batch sizes. [1]
